briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Growth Paths Emerge: Michigan Brands Expand and a Tax Fight Turns Political, While Psychedelics Race Toward FDA Approval
briefs.top: Michigan operators are finding real upside this week — national edibles brands are landing on local shelves, a Muskegon hospitality concept is pushing forward, and the 24% wholesale tax has become a genuine campaign issue with a real shot at relief. Nationally, cannabis M&A is consolidating fast and psychedelic medicine just cleared two more hurdles toward first-ever FDA approvals.

local.text: Grön, a Portland edibles brand owned by Wyld, announced its bestselling 'Pearls' gummies are now being sold in Michigan dispensaries as part of a four-state rollout, already confirmed on shelves at Pure Options, High Profile, and Lume. A solid proof point that national brands still see Michigan as a growth market worth prioritizing.

JARS Cannabis, the Michigan-based chain, announced a deal to acquire Sonoran Roots and its eight Ponderosa brand dispensaries, which will make JARS the largest dispensary chain in Arizona. A Michigan operator flexing multi-state muscle even as the home market tightens.

Fields Cannary's Muskegon buildout shows that ambitious hospitality-driven cannabis retail is still moving forward in the state, targeting a fall opening as a dispensary-restaurant concept — proof that experiential retail can still pencil out under the new tax regime.

Republican gubernatorial candidate John James has promised to repeal or cut Michigan's new 24% marijuana tax, and the industry is behind him — the Trump-endorsed nominee is telling the state's nearly $3.2 billion industry exactly what it wants to hear and collecting cash and support from Michigan marijuana operators in return, giving operators a real electoral lever for relief.

Michigan's 24% wholesale marijuana tax is still only bringing in a fraction of what state officials projected, generating about $37 million in Q2 2026 and roughly $34 million in Q1 against an initial estimate of $105 million per quarter — underperformance that strengthens the industry's case for rollback and adds fuel to the ongoing court fight and governor's race pressure.

national.text: A legal challenge to medical marijuana's Schedule III reclassification was rebuffed this week — on Sept. 9, 2026, the D.C. Circuit court left the rescheduling order in effect, finding opponents hadn't demonstrated grounds to overturn it, locking in the 280E tax relief operators have been counting on.

The FDA granted Compass Pathways' NDA rolling review request and selected COMP360 synthetic psilocybin for the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher program for treatment-resistant depression, with 39% of patients achieving a clinically meaningful response after two doses of psilocybin — an effect maintained for an average of six months, putting the first classic-psychedelic approval within sight for 2026-27.

The FDA's September 2026 NEJM framework for psychedelic drugs reshapes trial design, REMS requirements, and patient access for psilocybin and MDMA therapies, signaling a REMS-forward posture for future approvals — the clearest regulatory roadmap yet for how these medicines reach patients.

Curaleaf issued a new missive this week in its ongoing bid to woo Aurora Cannabis shareholders, keeping alive one of the biggest cross-border consolidation plays in cannabis as major operators bulk up for the next growth phase.

Cresco Labs has completed its $50 million acquisition of nine operational Pennsylvania medical marijuana dispensaries, giving the company full ownership after supporting the locations under a management agreement since April — another sign that well-capitalized MSOs are still actively expanding footprint even as smaller operators consolidate or exit.
